common.unexpected: Unexpected interface error: retry; if it persists, check the service logs.

cause.policy_rejected_all: every candidate rejected by the policy
cause.lease_busy: target already held by another operation
cause.operation_not_allowed: operation not allowed by the policy

exploitation.title: Operations desk
exploitation.lede: State of the selected target, the autonomous operation in progress, incidents and recovery. Decisions come from the versioned policy and the measurements, never from a click or an agent.
exploitation.noTarget: No target declared: run `field-horizon db bench-setup` or fill in the targets file (Settings).

launch.title: Start an autonomous optimization
launch.autonomy: Once started, the operation runs to its end with no further approval: measure, decide, retain or compensate. It keeps running if you close this window.
launch.workloadSummary: {{queries}} queries, {{writes}} of them writes (rolled back after measurement) and {{controls}} control.
launch.llm: Consult the LLM agents (advisory: never part of a decision)
launch.candidatesHelp: They go through exactly the same policy and measurement as every other candidate. No SQL is accepted.
launch.willRecover: Blocking incidents exist: automatic recovery will handle them before any change when ownership is proven — otherwise the operation is blocked with its diagnostic.
launch.willBlock: Blocking incidents exist and automatic recovery is off: the operation will be blocked. Run a recovery first.
launch.blockedReadOnly: This target is read-only: the policy allows no write in this environment.
launch.blockedReconciling: Start-up reconciliation in progress: no change is accepted until it ends.
launch.blockedIdentity: The instance does not prove its identity (marker or system identifier mismatch).

running.title: Operation in progress
running.browserNote: The operation runs in the service, not in this browser: closing the window does not stop it.

controls.label: Operation controls
controls.safePoint: Pause and cancel take effect at the next safe point (between steps or measurement rounds), never inside a DDL statement.
controls.pausedNote: Paused: the target stays reserved (lease kept). Authorization is re-verified before any later change.
controls.cancelling: Cancel requested: it applies at the next safe point; a change already applied will be removed (compensation confirmed in the catalog).
controls.cancelBody: The cancel applies at the next safe point. If the index was already built, it is removed by compensation, confirmed in the catalog. A DDL statement in progress is not interrupted. A cancel arriving after retention has no effect, and the sheet will say so.

incidents.title: Incidents and recovery
incidents.modes: Read-only detection on every refresh. Automatic recovery runs at service start and before any new operation; the button triggers a manual recovery. Only changes whose ownership is proven are removed.
incidents.confirmBody: Recovery takes the target lease, waits (bounded by the policy) for orphaned server activity to end, then removes only the indexes that the ledger, their structure and their marker (or an interrupted build) prove to be Field Horizon changes. Anything ambiguous is left in place and reported.

indexes.title: Field Horizon indexes on the target
indexes.help: Read live from the catalog and matched against the target's change ledger.
indexes.none: No Field Horizon index on this target.

startup.title: Start-up reconciliation
startup.none: No reconciliation recorded for this target since the service started.

operations.title: Operations
operations.lede: Every optimization and recovery run on the target, with its status and cause.

sheet.title: Operation sheet
sheet.finishedNoControls: Operation finished: no control applies any more.
sheet.noDecision: No decision: the operation ended before measuring a change.

decision.rule: Policy v{{version}}: the change is retained only if every criterion passes. Thresholds live in the versioned policy file; they are never adjusted after the fact.
decision.weightedNote: Sum of weight × median server time: a cost, not a throughput.
decision.sideEffectsNote: Measured writes are rolled back, yet leave dead tuples and consume identity values. A VACUUM before each phase restores the same starting point.
decision.sideEffectsLine: {{dead}} dead tuples, {{ids}} identity values consumed, {{bytes}} size change

measure.title: Server samples, before and after
measure.units: Server time = PostgreSQL execution time (EXPLAIN ANALYZE), which the decision uses. Client time = round trip of the plain statement, reported beside it.
measure.none: No measurement recorded for this operation.

authority.reverificationNote: Identity, policy file, target file, fresh facts and eligibility were checked again here; the executor refuses any authorization older than the policy's limit.
authority.compensationNote: Index removed by the executor after an ownership proof, then confirmed in the catalog and in the plans.
authority.plansClean: No plan uses it any more

agents.title: Agent claims, checked against the evidence
agents.note: Relevance, assertions and verdict are separate. What cannot be tested stays “unverifiable”. None of this enters a decision.
agents.none: Agents were not consulted for this operation.

evidence.note: Each file is hashed into the journal when written. Verify recomputes the hashes and the decision; export produces a redacted archive (literals masked, local paths hidden).
evidence.name: File
evidence.meaning: Integrity proves the files did not change since they were written, on this machine; it is not an independent attestation. A recomputation never replaces the recorded decision: both are shown.

evidencePage.title: Evidence and audit
evidencePage.lede: What the evidence proves, and what it does not.
evidencePage.integrityText: each file matches the sha256 recorded when it was written (same machine: not an attestation).
evidencePage.recomputeText: the decision is recomputed from the raw samples with the archived policy; the original is never replaced.
evidencePage.attestationText: none: no third party signed or timestamped this evidence.
evidencePage.redactionText: redacted by default; lab data is synthetic (generated, setseed 0.42) and labelled as such.

targets.title: Targets
targets.lede: Declared targets, what they are, and what the server proves live.
targets.identitiesNote: The observer and measurement identities hold no owner right; the operator reaches the owner only through an explicit SET ROLE, and only the executor holds its secret.
targets.boundaryNote: This table is read from the server's catalogs on every display: it is what PostgreSQL enforces, not what the application claims.
targets.residual: Declared residual power: under SET ROLE the operator keeps what no trigger intercepts (SELECT on lab data, LOCK, VACUUM, ANALYZE, CLUSTER) and can create, comment or drop template-conformant fhx_ indexes. Its secret is readable by any process of the current Windows user: Windows identity separation is not achieved on this workstation (administrator rights unavailable).
targets.trafficNote: Normalised statistics: they inform diagnosis; they are never replayed.

workloads.title: Workloads and performance
workloads.lede: What is measured (versioned files) and what the measurements concluded, per workload.
workloads.noRuns: Not measured on this target yet.

methodItems.rounds: Repeated rounds, rotated query order, identical parameters before and after (fixed seeds).
methodItems.aa: Noise bounded by an A/A comparison of the two baseline halves.
methodItems.controls: Control queries the index cannot serve: if they move, the environment drifted and nothing is credited.
methodItems.vacuum: VACUUM of the lab tables before each phase: every phase starts from the same state (no inherited dead tuples).
methodItems.settle: Bounded wait for running maintenance (autovacuum) to end before measuring.
methodItems.client: Client time measured and reported beside server time, outside the decision.
methodItems.writes: Writes always rolled back; their traces (dead tuples, identity values) are measured and reported.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Locations, the policy in force and what each control means. No secret is displayed.
settings.noSecrets: Secrets stay in the libpq password file (owner-only ACL); neither its content nor its path is shown here.
settings.policyReadOnly: Read-only here: the policy is a versioned file. Any edit changes its hash, and a running operation refuses it (policy_changed).
